title: Chicken Biryani
subtitle: Hyderabadi layered spiced rice with marinated chicken
excerpt: The great celebration rice of the Indian subcontinent: long-grain basmati rice layered with fragrant marinated chicken, caramelised onions, saffron, and whole spices, then sealed and cooked by the dum method so the steam perfumes every grain.

recipe.sourceNotes: Biryani is a rice dish with Persian roots (the word derives from the Persian birian, meaning fried before cooking) brought to the Indian subcontinent by Mughal rulers. There are dozens of distinct regional styles: Hyderabadi biryani (the most famous), Lucknowi (Awadhi) biryani, Kolkata biryani (which includes potatoes, introduced when local markets were expensive), and many others. The technique of dum (slow-cooking in a sealed vessel) is central to biryani: the rice and meat are layered and the pot is sealed with dough or foil so the steam circulates and cooks everything by trapped heat alone. This produces light, separate, fragrant grains and tender, deeply spiced meat. Biryani is a celebration dish across South Asia; it would be served at weddings, Eid, and special family gatherings.

content.text: Par-cook the rice to exactly 70 percent done before layering; it must retain firmness to absorb the steam and cooking juices without going mushy. Fry the onions very slowly until they are deeply caramelised and nearly crisp; they are both a flavouring and a garnish. Seal the pot tightly with foil before putting on the lid; no steam must escape.

items.preparation: bone-in thighs; cut into 2 pieces each
soaked in cold water for 30 minutes; drained
finely sliced; 2 for caramelising, 1 for the chicken base

content.text: Marinate the chicken in yoghurt, garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli, and 1 tsp salt for at least 1 hour. Fry 2 sliced onions in 4 tablespoons of oil over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until deeply golden and nearly crisp. Drain on paper and set aside. Par-boil the drained rice in heavily salted boiling water with the whole spices for 5 minutes until just starting to soften; drain immediately.

In a heavy-based pot, heat the remaining oil. Cook the remaining sliced onion for 5 minutes. Add the marinated chicken and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring. The chicken should be partially cooked and the sauce thick. Taste and adjust the salt.

Spread the par-cooked rice over the chicken in an even layer. Pour the saffron milk over the rice in threads. Scatter with the caramelised onions and coriander. Dot with butter. Cover tightly with foil, then the lid. Cook over the lowest possible heat for 25 to 30 minutes. Remove from the heat and leave to rest for 10 minutes before removing the lid. Gently fold together before serving.
